source_excerpts.text:
The strongest result is a fully written, internally reconstructed mixed-state classicalization theorem.

For every channel \(B:H\to H\otimes H\), one fixed measure-and-prepare channel \(\Lambda_B\) satisfies, simultaneously for every density matrix \(\rho\),

\[ 1-F(\rho,\Lambda_B(\rho)) \le 2800\,[1-F(B(\rho),\rho\otimes\rho)]. \]

Here \(F\) is squared Uhlmann fidelity. The measurement has at most \(2d\) rank-one outcomes. The proof combines a quadratic discrimination-risk gap, deletion induction, constrained amplification, and spectral polar rounding.

The independent-product premise is essential: an explicit counterexample has marginal broadcasting error tending to zero while every classical reconstruction has average infidelity tending to one.

The account also contains sharp Gaussian transport stability—including the logarithmic phase \(\min\{1/3,r/(r+1)\}\)—and an exact finite-semigroup coupling obstruction.

The mission’s major foundational-breakthrough standard remains unmet. Historical originality, external validation, and a transformative capability with complete acquisition costs are unestablished. The universal classifier’s acquisition and circuit complexity remain unknown.
